import cv2
import numpy as np
img = cv2.imread('painting.jpg').astype(np.float32)
h, w = img.shape[:2]

GW, GH = 48, 30
small = cv2.resize(img, (GW, GH), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
B,G,R = small[...,0], small[...,1], small[...,2]
# classify each cell
def cls(b,g,r):
    if r>150 and g>150 and b>150: return 'W'   # white/bright
    if r>150 and g>120 and b<120: return 'O'   # orange/warm bright
    if r>160 and g>140 and b<90:  return 'Y'   # yellow
    if b>g and b>r and b>90: return 'B'        # blue
    if b>r and b>g and b<90: return 'b'        # dark blue/navy
    if g>r and g>b: return 'G'                 # green
    if r>g and r>b: return 'R'                 # red/brown
    if r<40 and g<40 and b<40: return '.'      # near black
    if r>100 and g>90 and b>80 and abs(r-g)<25 and abs(g-b)<25: return '#' # gray
    return 'm'
out=[]
for y in range(GH):
    row=''
    for x in range(GW):
        row += cls(B[y,x], G[y,x], R[y,x])
    out.append(row)
print('\n'.join(out))
print()
# Also luminance map (darker chars = darker)
gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
g2 = cv2.resize(gray, (GW, GH), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
chars = ' .:-=+*#%@'
print('LUMINANCE:')
for y in range(GH):
    print(''.join(chars[min(9, int(g2[y,x]/256*10))] for x in range(GW)))
